Assistant
SC09 roof takeoff (read-only)

Geometry

Columns across the 8 m width: ⌈8 / 0.8⌉ = 10 sheets per course. Effective cover 0.8 m already includes side lap — do not deduct it twice.
Sheets per column along the run: 5 m ordered length, 0.2 m end lap ⇒ effective step per upper course = 4.8 m.

First-course-full rule The eaves (lowest) course is laid with full 5 m sheets — no end-lap deduction on its leading edge. Every higher course then advances only (sheet length − end lap) = 4.8 m up the run.

Counts at run = 9.8 m

Course 1 (full): 0 → 5.0 m.
Course 2: 5.0 → 9.8 m, closing the run exactly.
10 columns × 2 courses = 20 sheets = 100 linear metres ordered.

Course-count boundaries

Run = 5.0 m: 1 course (the full first course alone closes the run).
Run just above 5.0 m: 2 courses — any excess forces a second full sheet per column.
Run = 9.8 m: 2 courses close the run exactly.
Run just above 9.8 m: 3 courses — sheets per column rise to 3, ordered length jumps to 30 × 5 = 150 linear metres.

This is an internal draft; it is not a quote or engineering certification.

Developer review
Outcome — answered the rule, counts (10 × 2 = 20 sheets = 100 m), and the four boundary cases within the cap; flagged draft status.
Friction — at "just above 5 m" the second course still uses one full sheet per column; a reader focused on run-overlap may miss the sheet count jump.
Improvement — show per-column stacking at 9.8 m (full + full, one end lap) to make the count unambiguous.

value.reply:
Assistant

Whole vs filtered totals

Whole = every export line. Filtered = subset (e.g. items on Walls).
A and C sit under Walls; B is unassigned (whole only); D sits on Building only.

Don't sum inclusive parent + child

Building is Walls' parent. Building's inclusive rollup already contains A and C. Adding "Building total" to "Walls total" double-counts A and C. Pick one rule: child-only sum OR inclusive rollup — not both.

Flat item-only CSV

One row per measured item. Sum all rows, grouped by unit. m² rows together; lm rows together; never mix.

Hierarchical CSV (SUMMARY_NODE vs LEAF_ITEM)

SUMMARY_NODE = container rollup, derived from descendants. LEAF_ITEM = individual measured item.
Sum LEAF_ITEMs only. Never add SUMMARY_NODE values — they would re-add the same children.

Units and evidence classes

m² leaves: A 0.10 + B 0.20 + D 4.00 = 4.30 m² (unverified/inferred, kept separate).
lm leaves: C = 3 lm (sample). Never sum m² + lm.

Apostrophe protecting `=1+1`

A cell starting with =, +, -, @ or TAB is parsed as a formula and evaluates (e.g. to 2). Prefixing with a single apostrophe ('=1+1) is the CSV escape for literal text — the item name survives import as the string "=1+1".

Status: internal draft, quote-ineligible (verifiedQuoteEligible=false).

Developer review
Outcome — explained whole/filtered, double-count trap, flat vs hierarchical sums, unit/evidence separation, and the '=1+1 escape within the word cap; marked draft/quote-ineligible.
Friction — "inclusive rollup" may be read as "everything assigned anywhere", missing that Building's rollup already covers Walls.
Improvement — add one worked line: Building m² inclusive = A 0.10 + B 0.20 + D 4.00 = 4.30 m²; Walls filtered = A 0.10 m² + 3 lm — locks the rule.
